rows.title: Protesters arrested as Lamont, lawmakers strike CT budget deal
rows.standfirst: With a budget centered on middle-class tax relief largely finalized Thursday, protesters were still demanding more spending on wages.

rows.title: GOP objects as Lamont tries to resurrect waste disposal fee
rows.standfirst: Negotiations on the state budget have been complicated by a late move by Gov. Lamont to include new municipal waste fees in the budget.

rows.title: CT never spent $30 million it reserved to help the poor stay warm this winter
rows.standfirst: Money lawmakers set aside for the CT Energy Assistance Program remains unspent, even though requests for help were up 24% this winter.

rows.title: CT House adopts $51B budget with big middle-class tax cut
rows.standfirst: The CT budget proposal features an income tax cut and boosts funding to local schools. The Senate is expected to debate the bill on Tuesday.

rows.title: Senate gives overwhelming bipartisan approval to new CT budget
rows.standfirst: A new CT budget cuts income tax rates and invests in local schools but leaves questions around higher education and social services.

rows.title: Lawmakers send $7.5B bipartisan bond package to Lamont’s desk
rows.standfirst: The General Assembly OK’d a $7.5 billion two-year bond deal that invests in transportation, housing, higher education and school construction.

rows.title: The disabled have had long waits for services. That could change
rows.standfirst: Waiting lists have plagued CT’s disabled for years. Advocates hope latest effort to aid those with developmental disabilities isn’t a one-off.

rows.title: Harmonious CT budget sets stage for spending cap battle in 2024
rows.standfirst: The prospects of future CT budgets will likely hinge on how well Gov. Lamont works with his fellow Democrats on the “fiscal guardrails.”

rows.title: CT union to end weekslong strike at group homes
rows.standfirst: SEIU 1199NE will end the strike at group homes for clients with developmental disabilities, but says limited state funds blocked pay goal.

rows.title: CT advocates launch yearlong wage theft campaign
rows.standfirst: Supporters will push CT legislators to combat wage theft by hiring more wage and hour inspectors amid a months-long backlog of cases.

rows.title: CT bond commission approves another bailout for New London pier project
rows.standfirst: This marks the latest increase for the pier development — which originally was priced at $93 million in 2019.
